question: Does a light hierarchy traversed by the crossing test remove the many-light crossing cost on many-lights-v1 with equal images, small memory and build cost, and no low-light-count regression?
procedure: lotus-headless --benchmark, many-lights-v1, MIS, 64 bounces, 8 warmup + 64 measured frames, 128 and 512 pixels, Reference and Wavefront, light grid sides 1/2/4/8/16, --benchmark-light-crossing linear and hierarchy, 3 fresh processes per configuration in run-major round-robin order; rerun of 512-pixel sides 1 and 8 in 3 more processes; validation and synchronization validation active; clocks unlocked, nvidia-smi pstates sampled every 250 ms; lowest process medians are used

pinpoint.note: Reference 512 px, interleaved process pairs, no telemetry: side 1 linear, side 1 hierarchy, side 2 hierarchy, 4 rounds

build_cost.note: Copy of BoundLight/StoreBounds/BuildLightNode/BuildLightHierarchy compiled cl /O2 /std:c++20; host CPU time per build of grid sphere lights

decision: adopt: LightCrossing::Hierarchy default; Linear kept as evaluation baseline
